title: SlimSLAM: An Adaptive Runtime for Visual-Inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping
problem: SLAM algorithms must achieve both speed and accuracy for real-time performance in AR/VR and robotics, but accurate SLAM is computationally expensive while platforms are resource-constrained. Designers face a trade-off: pay for specialized accelerators or sacrifice algorithm accuracy.
motivation: Accurate SLAM is essential to prevent motion sickness in AR/VR headsets and navigation errors in autonomous robots and drones, yet computational constraints prevent real-time execution on typical platforms.
method: SlimSLAM uses an adaptive runtime that dynamically adjusts visual-inertial SLAM algorithm execution based on available computational resources. The system modulates algorithm functionality and complexity to meet real-time constraints while preserving pose estimation accuracy.
key_novelty: An adaptive runtime that maintains real-time SLAM performance across resource-constrained platforms by dynamically tuning algorithm workload.
contributions: Adaptive runtime framework for visual-inertial SLAM
Dynamic algorithm tuning mechanism to balance accuracy and latency
Real-time SLAM support on constrained platforms without specialized hardware
